stem: A 4-year-old boy presents for a planned health check and immunisations. He walked at 2 years and is still unsteady on his feet. He had delayed speech, which his mother says runs in the family. Examination shows large calves, a waddling gait, a positive Gowers manoeuvre, proximal weakness, and normal sensation, cranial nerves, coordination, tone, and cardiovascular examination. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: The combination of delayed motor milestones, Gowers sign, calf pseudohypertrophy, waddling gait, and proximal weakness is classic for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
rationale: Duchenne muscular dystrophy is the best fit because the child has proximal myopathy with calf pseudohypertrophy and Gowers sign. Mild developmental delay alone would not explain these examination findings.

optionExplanations.A: Developmental dysplasia of the hips can cause a limp, but does not explain Gowers sign, calf enlargement, or proximal muscle weakness.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: Duchenne muscular dystrophy causes proximal weakness, calf pseudohypertrophy, waddling gait, and Gowers sign in a young boy.
optionExplanations.C: Familial delay may explain mild delayed milestones, but not progressive weakness or calf pseudohypertrophy.
optionExplanations.D: Spina bifida occulta may be associated with subtle neurological findings, but not the classic muscular dystrophy picture described here.

Instructions

Question 3 - 5 relate to this quiz

Case 2

A 4 year old boy visits presents to you for his planned health check and immunisations. You have never met him before. You enquire about his developmental history and learn that he walked at 2 years and is still not very stable on his feet. He also didn’t start talking until he was 22 months which his mum says ‘runs in the family’. His mother is not concerned about his hearing or vision. He has an elder sister who is 6 and is thriving in school.

On examination the boy is not dysmorphic. His weight is 15kg (25th centile) and his height is 97cm (25th centile). His head circumference is 48cm (25th centile). When you examine his gait you notice he has very large calves and he walks with a waddling gait. When you get him to rise up from lying on the floor, he turns himself over and then uses his hands to push himself up from the floor. His tone is normal; his power is 4/5 proximally at the hips and shoulders but normal peripherally. You elicit deep tendon reflexes with reinforcement. His cranial nerve exam is normal. His coordination is normal as is his sensory exam. His cardiovascular examination is normal.
